description: Widen the mixed512 shape-6 (~105ms, biggest board cost) structural peel to route MORE of the batch off the cuSOLVER rest onto fast paths. brief-56 batched the rest through a C=3 cluster; brief-58 showed n=1024 rest cant be batched-beaten, but shape-6 is n=512 where the cluster/low-rank/two-level fast paths DO beat cuSOLVER. Re-sweep the peel windows (_MIXED_PEEL_PR_LO/HI dense, _MIXED_PEEL_PSD_PR_LO/HI, _MIXED_PEEL_CLUSTERED via _twolevel_mask) so a larger fraction of the 640-matrix batch is captured by dense-low-rank / psd-low-rank / two-level / cluster instead of falling to per-matrix cuSOLVER syevd. Each captured matrix moves from ~0.85ms cuSOLVER to a faster batched path. Per-matrix residual-gated; verify 0 new fallback. Pure torch.

rankdef peel PR[62,90) k=384 power=2 (0 fallback isolated) added to mixed512 peel. Isolated LR 20.9ms vs cuSOLVER 32.9ms (+12ms) BUT end-to-end shape6 107.29->109.15ms (+1.86ms slight LOSS): removing 77 mats from the brief-56 batched cluster does not shrink the cluster kernel proportionally while LR adds ~21ms+CQR2/gather. The rest's marginal cost per matrix under the batched cluster is far below the 0.85ms/mat cuSOLVER the peel math assumed. 39/39 validate.

rowscale peel PR[0,33) k=192 power=1 isolated (rankdef OFF). Isolated LR 13.8ms vs cuSOLVER 27.8ms (+14ms) BUT end-to-end shape6 107.29->118.02ms (+10.7ms LOSS, worse than rankdef). Same mechanism as t1: the brief-56 batched cluster handles the rest at a marginal cost far below the LR path's fixed CQR2 floor, so peeling mats OFF the cluster to LR costs more than it saves. 39/39 validate.

rankdef+rowscale peels BOTH ON (123 mats off the cluster). End-to-end shape6 107.29->120.66ms (+13.4ms LOSS, worst of t1/t2/t3, losses stack). Decisive: the brief-56 batched cluster handles the rest at a marginal per-matrix cost BELOW the LR path's fixed CQR2 floor, so every matrix peeled cluster->LR is a net loss. The 0.85ms/mat cuSOLVER premise no longer holds (brief-56 already replaced it). 39/39 validate.

KEEPER (rankdef/rowscale peels OFF) == parent behavior: geomean 28580us (~= parent 28621, noise), shape6 107.17ms (~= 107.29), shape3 78.03ms unaffected. MEASURED NEGATIVE FINDING: mixed512 shape-6 capture is already ~638-640/640 on fast batched paths; a 5-seed reseed sweep shows at most 2/640 mats reach per-matrix cuSOLVER (0 on 3/5 seeds) -- brief-56's batched cluster already swept the entire rest onto a fast path, so there is no cuSOLVER rest to widen into. Peeling rest subsets to LR is a net loss (t1/t2/t3) because the cluster's marginal per-matrix cost < the LR fixed CQR2 floor. Dense/psd windows re-swept: already optimally wide (widening catches +1/+0 mats). 39/39 validate, stream absent (0). Profile saved brief-73-trial-4-shape6.

brief-73 (widen mixed512 shape-6 peel) DONE. Branch HEAD fd3f5dbc8, geomean 28580us (== parent 697c7f51d 28621, within noise). KEEPER == parent routing (both new peel flags OFF), 39/39 validate, stream absent (0), shape3 unaffected (78.03ms).

MEASURED NEGATIVE FINDING (the brief's premise no longer holds): mixed512 shape-6 capture is ALREADY ~638-640/640 on fast batched paths. A 5-seed reseed sweep (770001/111111/424242/990099/222222) shows at most 2/640 matrices ever reach per-matrix cuSOLVER (exactly 0 on 3 of 5 seeds). brief-56's batched-cluster rest already swept the ENTIRE heterogeneous rest onto a fast path, so there is essentially NO per-matrix cuSOLVER 'rest' to widen into. The 'cuSOLVER 0.85ms/mat -> fast path' lever in the brief was closed by brief-56.

Per-path counts (parent, seed 770001, of 640): dense-LR[48,62)k352=264, psd-LR[37,48)k256=76, clustered-2lvl=37, batched-cluster-rest=263, per-matrix cuSOLVER=2. The 2 cuSOLVER matrices are cluster-gate fallbacks: idx66 (orth3441/eig2744 units, genuinely unresolvable by the FP16 cluster reduction) + idx245 (eig111<200 harness but orth135>75 internal gate).

Peeling rest subsets to a dedicated low-rank path was measured a NET LOSS at every widening: rankdef PR[62,90)k384p2 0-fallback (t1 shape6 107.29->109.15ms +1.86ms), rowscale PR[0,33)k192p1 0-fallback (t2 +10.7ms), both (t3 +13.4ms). Mechanism (nsys + scaling probe): the batched cluster kernel is 45ms for 263 mats and DOES scale ~with count, but its marginal per-matrix cost is BELOW the low-rank path's fixed CQR2 floor (trsm/potrf/syrk ~15ms + gather/scatter), so moving mats cluster->LR pays more than it saves. Confirmed dense/psd are much cheaper on LR than cluster (dense 33 vs 56ms, psd 12 vs 19ms) and one big cluster over everything (152ms) loses to the current split (126ms) -- the existing architecture is well-tuned.

Dense/psd windows re-swept for reseed margin: dense mass cleanly at PR[52,58), widening to [44,62) or [48,70) catches +1 matrix; psd mass at [40,44], widening to [33,48) catches +0 (rowscale is a clean gap below at [25,29]). Windows already optimally wide.

OPEN DIRECTIONS for a follow-up brief (NOT widening -- these attack the captured paths' COST, the real remaining lever on shape 6's 107ms): (1) the batched-cluster rest kernel is 45ms/263mats (44.6% of shape 6) -- re-sweep _REST_CLUST_C / _REST_NS_STEPS for the ACTUAL rest composition, or a cheaper reduced-precision cluster; (2) ~47ms of shape-6 time is CQR2/gate/gather overhead (trsm/potrf/syrk + index_copy/scatter) spread across the dense-LR + psd-LR + rest-cluster calls -- fuse or reduce the per-call gate GEMMs / NS steps; (3) the single idx245 orth-only cluster fallback could be salvaged with a targeted NS rescue on the cluster path (mirrors brief-67's LR rescue) for ~0.85ms, but that is noise-level. The dominant lever is the 45ms cluster kernel + the 47ms overhead, not capture width.
